Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):

]

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant now runs to "Company and its affiliates (on written notice to Contractor)"; "Company" is defined in the preamble as Clear Capital only, so the added words supply genuinely new affiliate coverage rather than duplicating an existing definition.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 4(c) as rendered names only "Company and its affiliates"; no words extend the grant to contractors or other third parties acting on Company's behalf. The pre-existing sublicensing right is a discretionary right to grant sublicences, not an express licence to Company's contractors.

elements.element: A paid-up licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Retained language grants a "royalty-free, non-exclusive perpetual license" — the licence is fully paid-up (royalty-free) and expressly perpetual.

elements.element: A paid-up licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The grant says "royalty-free, non-exclusive perpetual" but nowhere says "irrevocable"; the drafter would need to insert "irrevocable" into the string of licence adjectives in Section 4(c).

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: the only licence in the document is a royalty-free perpetual grant of Contractor's Information incorporated into the Works; there is no subscription or term-limited licence for this restriction to attach to.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The insertion is limited to "a successor in a merger or acquisition without Contractor's approval". Read literally that is narrower than transferability to Customer's successors generally (e.g. successor by asset sale, reorganisation or operation of law); the drafter would need to broaden to "transferable to Customer's successors and assigns" for the preferred element.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "Contractor hereby grants to Company and its affiliates (on written notice to Contractor) a royalty-free, non-exclusive perpetual license" — affiliate coverage with the written-notice mechanic exactly as the fallback requires.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition without Contractor's approval" is inserted into the operative grant, and the express no-approval wording neutralises the general consent requirement in Section 10 for this transfer.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: affiliate coverage on written notice and M&A successor transferability are both inside the Section 4(c) grant, not merely promised in the margin comment.

Preferred level fails on three elements: no contractor coverage, no "irrevocable", and successor transferability narrowed to M&A only. To reach preferred the drafter would add "and its contractors acting on its behalf", insert "irrevocable" among the licence adjectives, and broaden "a successor in a merger or acquisition" to Customer's successors generally.

Minimality holds: only the two fallback features were added to an existing grant; the favourable retained terms (royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable, business-operations scope) are untouched, nothing outside the checklist (no survival tail, expense or procedure language) is added, and no word was deleted.
The "without Contractor's approval" tag is the permitted direct form rather than a broad notwithstanding override of Section 10, so it does not breach the minimality boundary on assignment overrides.

Intent preserved: Section 10 is left intact and is not contradicted — it governs assignment of the Agreement and its obligations, whereas the new words permit transfer of a specific licence right; no new assignment exception is granted to Contractor, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("affiliates" is used in its ordinary sense, consistent with the Agreement's undefined usage).
Minor drafting nit for the record, not a failure: "a successor" is unqualified as to which party's successor; "a successor to Company" would remove any ambiguity.

input.quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs indefinitely (§ 2: "shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and the only convenience right, in § 6(a), is available solely "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding". Once an engagement is under way — precisely when an exit matters — Company has no right to terminate for convenience, and § 6(b) is confined to uncured material breach. That absence of any Customer convenience right in an open-ended term fails both the preferred and fallback positions, and the fallback's "end of a term" anchor has no application in an indefinite MSA. We therefore added, at the preferred level, an express right in operative language for Company to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on thirty (30) days' advance written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any Statement of Work is outstanding (mutually exclusive with retained § 6(a), so Contractor's 15-day right survives only when nothing is in progress). Sections 2, 6(a) and 6(b) are preserved verbatim, including the Customer-favourable mutual 15-day gap-period right.

We added a Company right to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirmed Contractor cannot walk away mid-engagement.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

input.quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs indefinitely (§ 2: "shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and the only convenience right in § 6(a) is available solely "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding". So once an engagement is under way — precisely when an exit matters — Company has no right to terminate for convenience, and § 6(b) is limited to uncured material breach. That absence of any Customer convenience right in an open-ended term fails both the preferred and fallback positions, and the fallback's "end of a term" mechanic has no application in an indefinite MSA. We therefore added, at the preferred level, a Company convenience right on thirty (30) days' notice over the Agreement or any Statement of Work with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any Statement of Work is outstanding (consistent with the retained § 6(a) limitation, so Contractor's 15-day right survives only when nothing is in progress).

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C), preferred-level cure.**

- **Issue:** § 6(a) allows convenience termination only "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding," and § 2 makes the term open-ended. Clear Capital therefore has no convenience exit once an engagement is running, and § 6(b) covers only uncured material breach — failing both preferred and fallback (whose "end of a term" mechanic is inapplicable to an indefinite MSA).
- **Cure:** one inserted subsection 6(c) giving Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any SOW is outstanding. RadialSpark's residual 15-day right (only when nothing is in progress) and all other § 6 text are preserved verbatim.

elements.evidence: Paragraph 1(b) states "Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards" — a performance covenant, not a representation or warranty; the inserted warranty sentence warrants only conformity to "the requirements of this Agreement" for 30 days and contains no professional/workmanlike warranty. To meet this element the drafter would need an express "Contractor warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" statement.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "each software deliverable included in the Works will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery" for software deliverables, not twelve (12) months.

elements.element: The Services warranty lasts 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted Services warranty runs "for thirty (30) days following performance", short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "at Contractor's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software deliverable or Services".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "or a refund of the fees paid for them".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained 5(a): Contractor "represents and warrants ... that Contractor's performance of the Services ... does not and shall not violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation". The "to its knowledge" qualifier weakens it below the preferred unqualified standard but an express legal-compliance warranty exists.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No anti-malicious-code warranty appears in Section 5, in paragraph 1(b), or in the inserted sentence; a separate "no viruses, malware or other malicious code" warranty would be required.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, each software deliverable included in the Works will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will conform to the requirements of this Agreement" — 30 days, meeting the floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software deliverable or Services".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "a refund of the fees paid for them".

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"preferred","mappings":[{"element":"Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
The Agreement runs indefinitely (§ 2: "shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and the only convenience right, in § 6(a), is available solely "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding". Once an engagement is under way — precisely when an exit matters — Company has no right to terminate for convenience, and § 6(b) is confined to uncured material breach. That absence of any Customer convenience right in an open-ended term fails both the preferred and fallback positions, and the fallback's "end of a term" anchor has no application in an indefinite MSA. We therefore added, at the preferred level, an express right in operative language for Company to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on thirty (30) days' advance written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any Statement of Work is outstanding (mutually exclusive with retained § 6(a), so Contractor's 15-day right survives only when nothing is in progress). Sections 2, 6(a) and 6(b) are preserved verbatim, including the Customer-favourable mutual 15-day gap-period right.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0032: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
p0033: (b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
p0011: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Effective Date: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Contractor: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Services: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

Rendered operative language:
2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
(a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
(b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
In addition to the foregoing rights, Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of such termination. Contractor may not terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience while any Statement of Work is outstanding.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] Section 6(a) only permits convenience termination when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so we have no exit once an engagement starts. We added a Company right to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirmed Contractor cannot walk away mid-engagement.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The retained clause requires "comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)" but states no per-occurrence basis; the limit basis is unspecified, so the per-occurrence anchor required by the element is absent.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate limit appears anywhere in clause 14 as rendered; only a single USD 1,000,000 CGL figure is stated.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O remains at "at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the USD 2,000,000 preferred limit.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cover is "cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", short of the USD 5,000,000 preferred limit; Contractor handles Company confidential records and systems, so the condition applies.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance ... evidencing the above coverage".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)".

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", operative for the term of the Agreement and covered by the existing certificates mechanic ("evidencing the above coverage").

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: the existing E&O limit of USD 1,000,000 already satisfies the first element, and the single inserted phrase adds unconditional cyber and privacy liability cover of USD 2,000,000, satisfying the second.

The preferred level is not reached: no per-occurrence basis for CGL, no USD 2,000,000 CGL aggregate, E&O still at USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000, and cyber at USD 2,000,000 rather than USD 5,000,000. To reach preferred the drafter would need to state "USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate", raise E&O to USD 2,000,000 and cyber to USD 5,000,000.

Minimality holds: the edit is a single conjunctive insertion into the existing sentence; workers' compensation, CGL, E&O, the "in connection with the provision of Services" scope, the certificates mechanic and the material-change notice are all retained verbatim, and no survival tail, at-own-expense language or other model-language extras were imported.

Intent is preserved: the new cover sits inside the existing term-long obligation and is captured by "evidencing the above coverage", leaving no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

With either party able to terminate for convenience on fifteen days' notice, the absence of any exit mechanics fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance and export within 30 days), so we insert a single paragraph at the preferred level: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter.

p0032: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

Services: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-ip-b7a45064","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.","rationale":"Section 4 is structured in our favour and meets the fallback in full (and most of the preferred). § 4(a) vests the \"Works\" (all drawings, documents, designs, inventions, programs, systems, data and documentation prepared by Contractor as Statement of Work product) in Clear Capital as \"the property of Company,\" and § 11(c) (p0044) adds an express assignment of all right, title and interest in Works in progress on termination once final payment is made. § 4(b)(i)-(ii) confines Contractor's retained ownership to its own pre-existing proprietary tools, methodologies, know-how and records — permitted generic-tools/know-how retention, not a deliverables grab. § 4(c) grants us a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivative versions of any embedded Contractor's Information for our business operations, and § 4(d) confirms we may modify the software and engage third parties to do so without further payment. Searches for \"exclusive\", \"sole provider/supplier\", \"requirements\", \"exclusively\", \"non-compete\", \"first refusal\" and \"right to match\" returned only (i) Contractor's ownership of its own pre-existing materials and a non-exclusive licence to Company (p0020, p0021), (ii) the \"complete and exclusive agreement\" entire-agreement recital (p0051), and (iii) a mutual employee non-solicitation (p0047) — none of which restricts Company's freedom to source services elsewhere. We therefore moved the law to New York and substituted exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County (with only temporary injunctive relief available elsewhere), renaming the retained Section 19 heading so no arbitration reference dangles.","proposal":"Move governing law to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive New York County court jurisdiction.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-8c97d479","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3 CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The compensation provisions (§ 3(a)-(c)) set Contractor's fees solely by reference to each Statement of Work on a time-and-materials basis, with a unilateral Contractor rate-change notice right; there is no most-favoured-nation, most-favoured-customer, best-terms, benchmarking or right-to-match mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. The clause therefore fails the fallback, which needs E&O of USD 1,000,000 (already met verbatim) plus cyber cover of USD 2,000,000. We target the fallback with the shortest possible edit: inserting cyber and privacy liability cover of USD 2,000,000 into the existing sentence and leaving every other coverage, the certificates mechanic and all untouched wording verbatim. We note only in passing (not as a deviation) that the preferred position would also add a CGL aggregate limit and higher E&O/cyber limits.","proposal":"Add cyber and privacy liability coverage of USD 2,000,000 to the existing insurance clause.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-b17f1ded","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.","rationale":"Section 7(a) caps both parties, but the basis is not 12 months' fees: Contractor's cap is only the fees paid for the particular Services under the relevant Statement of Work, which on a long or multi-SOW engagement can fall well below twelve months' fees. That fails the fallback on material terms. We therefore target the fallback: a mutual cap of fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, with Excluded Claims (indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) outside the cap. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor MSA — verified findings and redline positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Nine clauses are compliant, eight are deviations requiring redline, and two rules are unaddressed by the document.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us in the places that usually cost the most. Ownership of deliverables under § 4 sits at or above our fallback: the "Works" vest in Company, Contractor's retained rights are confined to its own pre-existing tools and know-how, and we take a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to any embedded Contractor Information. There is no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-compete, no audit right against us, no liquidated damages or exit fee, and no auto-renewal window we can miss (the term is evergreen with a mutual 15-day exit when no Statement of Work is outstanding).
